question: What does the independent Session verifier actually pay for a certificate?
scope: Source-derived public GameSession.submit call counts, not measured CPU/wall or a total primitive-cost model.

definitions.N: Number of visited tree-node occurrences in a successfully verified ordinary-action certificate, root included.
definitions.h0: Number of ordinary actions in the authoritative root GameRecord, not a guessed board-only ply.
definitions.di: Ordinary-edge depth of node occurrence i from the certificate root.
definitions.D: Maximum such depth; certificate rank is a checked strategy-depth bound, not alpha-beta uniform completed depth.

derivation: For each ordinary edge parent->child, GameSession.replay(parent_record) replays h0+d_parent actions, then execute submits the edge once: h0+d_child calls.
Sum over all nonroot edges plus the initial root replay. Distinct traversal occurrences count separately even if a Python subtree object were shared.

examples.scope: Conditional abstract certificate shapes only; no claim these exact shapes are realized by the frozen games. No engine/prover execution.

partial_and_failed: The exact equality is for a complete accepted ordinary-action tree. It cannot be inferred from a partial visit count alone.
Root admission replays h0 actions before the first verifier node is visited; zero nodes is not zero work.
A child replay/submit occurs before that child calls budget.visit. A node-budget stop may therefore have one completed transition beyond the count of newly visited nonroot nodes.
For V visited nodes and valid rank bound D, an outer-call upper estimate including that extra edge is (V+1)*h0+V*D; this excludes declaration/resignation operations and does not bound per-call work.
Full legal-defense enumeration, rule terminal/check computation, declaration assessment, Session initialization and metadata/record comparison are additional work not measured by submit count.
eager_batch: Batched PN calls legal_successors before iterating inspected children. With cap1 it may inspect only the root yet generate B authoritative board successors before stopping on the first child visit.
The existing eager_board_successors/transitions/frontiers fields expose different costs; replacing all of them by PN nodes is invalid.

Atomic public replay/Core batches poll before/after and may overrun the nominal phase deadline. Actual elapsed/censored returns must be preserved; this is an existing granularity contract, not a newly reproduced bug.
memory: Retained PN nodes keep full immutable state/record histories. Prefix entries can be shared while tuple reference arrays still grow with history.
No constant bytes-per-node or textbook depth-first memory advantage follows for the retained-tree threshold prototype; actual RSS remains UNKNOWN.
interpretation: This identifies why fixed PN/verifier visit budgets do not equate whole service. It does not establish that replay is a removable dominant cost or justify a new verifier/kernel/timing campaign.
